Incorporating the latest Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey (SLOOS) tilts the assessment more cautious than the initial read of the May 1 FOMC statement.

- Policy stance: The Fed held 5.25–5.50% and tapered QT (lower Treasury redemption cap). Language remains “balanced” on risks but requires greater confidence on inflation before cutting.
- SLOOS credit supply: Banks reported tightening across C&I and consumer credit—higher loan spreads, tighter terms and credit limits, and increased credit score requirements—driven by economic outlook, reduced risk tolerance, industry-specific concerns, and supervisory/accounting considerations.
- SLOOS demand: Banks reported weaker demand for C&I loans and softer consumer credit appetite; CRE loan demand remains subdued.
- CRE standards: CRE lending standards tightened further (wider spreads, lower LTVs, higher DSCRs, smaller loan sizes, shorter IO periods, narrowed market areas), reflecting concerns about rents, vacancies, and property prices.
- Macro-financial read-through: These credit headwinds restrain growth and should help disinflation over time, but they also raise downside risks for weaker borrowers and amplify vulnerabilities flagged in the FSR (CRE, corporate credit, MMFs, leveraged basis trades).
- Net: QT taper is a modest positive, but SLOOS indicates continued tightening in the credit channel. Relative to the prior “slightly positive” tone, the balance shifts toward neutral-to-slightly negative.
